reason: The named characters in this passage are predominantly presented as religious figures with significant status and divine importance. Samuel (שְׁמוּאֵל) is a young servant in the temple through whom God speaks directly as a prophet; Eli (עֵלִי) is explicitly a priest and judge who has served Israel for 40 years; and his sons Hophni and Phinehas (חָפְנִי וּפִֽינְחָֽס) are priests. While Samuel is described as a youth (נער), he is already serving before the Lord and is being called by God Himself in this passage, marking him as religiously significant rather than an ordinary person. The text emphasizes their divine encounters and religious roles rather than portraying any named characters as merely regular people engaged in common activities.
